Title: Change Pose by Collada's Joint Information
Content: Objective Note: Only available for file formats with avatar joint information. In this case, COLLADA is being used. As the avatar's joints move when the pose changes, it is possible to change the avatar's pose while keeping the simulation stable even if there is a large difference between the starting and ending poses. However, if the avatar is exported via DAZ Studio, some composition form information may be lost during the process. Therefore, it is necessary to load the posed avatar's OBJ file and adjust the garments after changing the pose. (The avatar's OBJ file only saves the composition form information, so there is no danger of losing information during the loading process.) Operation Export a T-pose avatar which can be easily draped and an avatar with the final pose in COLLADA files. To find out export methods from DAZ Studio and Poser in details, check 3D File (COLLADA) Import for the reference. After exporting the COLLADA files, export the avatar poses in OBJ files. Load a posed COLLADA file from the previously saved avatars in program. Click File Save Pose to save current avatar as POS file. After dressing T-pose avatar, this file is going to be used when changing current pose. Click File Open Avatar to open the previously saved T-pose COLLADA file. Dress the avatar with desired garments. Now Click File Open Pose to open the previously saved POS file. The avatar slowly changes poses. It may take a while depending on the complexity of the garments. After the pose changes, load an OBJ file without any loss and adjust garments. Click File Import OBJ to open the previously saved final pose OBJ file. Highly positive to observe garments being under the avatar's surface. While simulation is being activated, drag out the parts of the garment that are located under the surface of the avatar by using the left mouse button. To find more details in Select/Move tool, check Move Garment for the reference.

Title: Morph Target with AVT Files
Content: Objective Apply morph target function onto the AVT files to change the avatar Pose or shape. Location Main Menu File Open Avatar Main Menu File Add Avatar Operation Open an Avatar in the 3D window. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu File Open Avatar Main Menu File Add Avatar The Add Avatar or Open Avatar window appears. Select Load as Morph Target for the Load Type and select OK. If morphing succeeds, the first avatar Pose or shape changes to the second avatar Pose or shape. If morphing fails, a warning pop-up window appears and no change is made.

Title: Reset Joints
Content: Objective Reset avatar's joints back to before editing (ver2.3.0). Location 3D Window Right-click Pop-up Menu (On Avatar) Reset Joints Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: 3D Window Right-click Pop-up Menu (On Avatar) Reset Joints Avatar's joints reset.

Title: Play Motion
Content: Objective Play Pose(*.pos) or Motion(*.mtn) files. Location Main Menu Avatar Play Motion 2D Toolbar Play Motion Operation Pose Open a Pose file. When a Pose file is loaded, the Play Motion tool is automatically activated. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu Avatar Play Motion 2D Toolbar Play Motion Click the Play Motion tool while the Avatar changes pose. The Avatar stops temporarily. The Avatar changes pose again. Motion Open a Motion file. The Play Motion tool now can be selected. Click the Play Motion tool. The motion is played. * The Transition Animation for the default avatars of the version 10 is not compatible with the previous versions.

Title: AVATAR MEASUREMENT SETTING: Delete Tape Measure
Content: Objective Delete tape measures that are no longer in need. Location Main Menu Avatar Avatar Editor Measure Delete Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu Avatar Avatar Editor Measure Delete Select a tape measure to delete. Click on the Delete icon. The selected tape measure is now being deleted.

Title: AVATAR MEASUREMENT SETTING: Open/Save Tape Measure
Content: Objective Save a created tape measure in .mea file format. Open a saved tape measure to reuse it. Location Main Menu Avatar Avatar Editor Measure Open /Save Operation Open Measurement Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu Avatar Avatar Editor Measure Open Open File window appears. Select a desired file and click Open. Save Measurement Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu Avatar Avatar Editor Measure Save Save File window appears. Select a desired location to store. Enter a desired file name and click Save. .mea file is now being created.

Title: AVATAR MEASUREMENT SETTING: Show/Hide All Tape Measure
Content: Objective Show or hide all of the tape measures in the window. Location Main Menu Display Avatar Show Avatar Measurements 3D Window Avatar Display (Mouse-over) Show Avatar Measurements Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu Display Avatar Show Avatar Measurements 3D Window Avatar Display (Mouse-over) Show Avatar Measurements All Avatar tape measures are now being displayed or hidden.

Title: AVATAR MEASUREMENT SETTING: Show/Hide Individual Tape Measure
Content: Objective Show or hide tape measure individually. Location Main Menu Avatar Avatar Editor Measure Bottom of the Avatar Editor Window Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu Avatar Avatar Editor Measure Bottom of the Avatar Editor Window Click the check-box to turn it On or Off.

Title: AVATAR MEASUREMENT SETTING: Rearrange Tape Measure
Content: Objective Rearrange tape measure according to avatar size. Location Main Menu Avatar Avatar Editor Measure Fit to Avatar Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu Avatar Avatar Editor Measure Fit to Avatar Click on the Fit to Avatar icon. Tape measures are now being rearranged automatically to the avatar's size.

Title: AVATAR MEASUREMENT SETTING: Change Tape Measure Type
Content: Objective Change tape measure type to 'Basic' or 'Surface' as needed. Location Main Menu Avatar Avatar Editor Measure Bottom of the Avatar Editor Window Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu Avatar Avatar Editor Measure Bottom of the Avatar Editor Window The type of tape measure is now being changed as chosen.

Title: AVATAR CREATING MEASUREMENT: Height Measurement
Content: Objective Take avatar's height measurements from the ground to the relevant points. Location Main Menu Avatar Measurement Height Measurement Pop-up Menu (Right-click 3D window Toolbar) Measurement Toolbar (Hold left mouse button at least two seconds) Height Measurement Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu Avatar Measurement Height Measurement Pop-up Menu (Right-click 3D window Toolbar) Measurement Toolbar (Hold left mouse button at least two seconds) Height Measurement Click a point to take the height measurement. Double-click another point to end the height measurement. A light-green colored rectangle indicating the ground automatically appears, and a green line connecting the ground and the clicked point appears to indicate the height.

Title: AVATAR CREATING MEASUREMENT: Basic/Surface Tape Measurement
Content: Objective Take avatar's measurements such as arm length, back length from projected points. Basic Tape Measurement measures following by its surface curves. Location Main Menu Avatar Measurement Basic/Surface Tape Measurement Pop-up Menu (Right-click 3D window Toolbar) Measurement Toolbar (Hold left mouse button at least two seconds) Basic/Surface Tape Measurement Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu Avatar Measurement Basic/Surface Tape Measurement Pop-up Menu (Right-click 3D window Toolbar) Measurement Toolbar (Hold left mouse button at least two seconds) Basic/Surface Tape Measurement Click on a point to begin the length measurement. Temporary line appears in purple. Click on any points that need to be included in the process, and double click to end the measurement.

Title: AVATAR CREATING MEASUREMENT: Basic/Surface Circumference Measurement
Content: Objective Take avatar's circumference measurements by measuring its surface curves. There are two options for circumference measurement. Basic Circumference measurement simply measures its circumference. Surface Measurement measures exactly following avatar's shape. Location Main Menu Avatar Measurements Basic Circumference Measurement Pop-up Menu (Right-click 3D window Toolbar) Measurement Toolbar (Hold left mouse button at least two seconds) Basic/Surface Circumference Measurement Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu Avatar Measurements Basic Circumference Measurement Pop-up Menu (Right-click 3D window Toolbar) Measurement Toolbar (Hold left mouse button at least two seconds) Basic/Surface Circumference Measurement Click on one end of desired circumference measurement. Click on the other end. Mouse over a spot between the two points to set the circumference measurement angle. Temporary line appears in purple. Click when the desired angle of the circumference line appears.

Title: Attach to Avatar Tape  (ver. 5.1.4)
Content: Related articles Linear Avatar Tape Circumference Avatar Tape Delete Avatar Tape Objective Attach avatar tapes to internal or external seam/pattern lines. Location Main Menu Avatar Avatar Tape Attach to Avatar Tape 3D Toolbar Attach to Avatar Tape Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu Avatar Avatar Tape Attach to Avatar Tape 3D Toolbar Attach to Avatar Tape In the 3D window, select a seam or pattern line to attach to avatar tape. Pattern with the selected line becomes transparent and the selected line gets highlighted in red. Select avatar tape to be attached. Once it is selected, the pattern becomes normal, and the attached seam or pattern line and the avatar tape become red. To detach avatar tape from the seam or pattern line, click on Attach to Avatar Tape tool again, and press 'Delete' on the keyboard.

Title: Delete Avatar Tape  (ver. 5.1.4)
Content: Related articles Linear Avatar Tape Circumference Avatar Tape Attach to Avatar Tape Objective Delete avatar tapes. Location Main Menu Avatar Avatar Tape Edit Avatar Tape 3D Toolbar Edit Avatar Tape Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu Avatar Avatar Tape Edit Avatar Tape 3D Toolbar Edit Avatar Tape Click on a tape to delete. The tape is highlighted in yellow. Press Delete key on the keyboard. The selected tape is now being deleted.

Title: Linear Avatar Tape  (ver. 5.1.4)
Content: Related articles Circumference Avatar Tape Attach to Avatar Tape Delete Avatar Tape Objective Create a linear baseline to improve accuracy in fit and draping on the 3D window. Location Main Menu Avatar Avatar Tape Linear Avatar Tape 3D Toolbar Linear Avatar Tape Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu Avatar Avatar Tape Linear Avatar Tape 3D Toolbar Linear Avatar Tape Click to make the beginning point of the tape at a desired place. Blue dot appears and gets fixed. Note: Pressing the Shift key on the keyboard before creating the beginning point provides a guideline on the avatar. Click another place to make the second point. Another blue dot appears and gets fixed and a connected line between both of the dots appears. Double-click to complete.

Title: Delete Avatar
Content: Objective Select avatar and delete individually. Note: Versions below ver2.5.0 only allow avatar deletion for all. Location Main Menu Avatar Delete Avatar 3D Toolbar Select/Move Pop-up Menu (Right-click on Avatar) Delete Avatar Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu Avatar Delete Avatar 3D Toolbar Select/Move Pop-up Menu (Right-click on Avatar) Delete Avatar The avatar is now being deleted. Note: From ver2.5.0, deleted avatars can immediately be restored at Main Menu Edit Undo or Press (Ctrl+Z)

Title: Sansar Export
Content: Objective Export in the samd file format for use in Sansar. Location Main Menu File Export Sansar (Samd) Operation Find and click the menu indicated in Location. The Save File window follows. Enter the garment name into the File name tab and press Save to save the file. The file saves in the Sansar format.

Title: Animation Import
Content: Objective Import Animation cache data created in the third-party 3D solutions. Note: Refer to the links below for FBX/ Alembic file import:. 3D File (FBX) Import/Export 3D File (Alembic) Import/Export Location Main Menu File Import Animation Maya Cache(.mc) Maya Cache(.mcx) Point Cache 2 MDD Cache(Standard) MDD Cache(Maya/3ds Max) Cache(Maya/3ds Max) Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu File Import Animation Maya Cache (.mc) Maya Cache (.mcx) Point Cache 2 MDD Cache(Standard) MDD Cache (Maya/3ds Max) The File Explorer or Find window appears. Select the desired file and click OK. An option window appears with settings that apply to the file format selected. Set the following individual settings. Object Select All Avatars Apply the cache data to all objects in the 3D environment. Cache data can be applied to individual objects from the submenu. FPS Set the frame rate of the cache data. Note: This menu only appears when importing Point Cache (PC2) files. Scale Set the scale of the cache data. Axis Conversion Set the axis direction for the cache data. The Y-axis runs vertically by default. Garment Position Move Avatar &amp Garment to Start Position Moves the Avatar and Garment to the location of the first frame (ver2.5.0). Transition Animation A transition animation is an animation that changes from a T-pose to a motions first pose in stages, and is created when the avatars current pose and motion differs from that of the first frame pose. Click OK. The cache data is imported according to the selected settings.

Title: 3D Garment Information (Below ver4.0.0)
Content: Objective Document and check garment information in Garment/ Project files. Location Main Menu File Information Garment Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu File Information Garment The Garment Information window appears. Document information related to the file as needed. If you want to view the Garment information upon the start of the file, check Display When Garment File Loads option located on left bottom corner, and then click OK. Note: Garment information will be saved when you save the Garment/ Project file.

Title: 3D Garment Information (ver4.1.0 and Above)
Content: Objective Write and check important Garment information. Location Main Menu File Information Garment Operation Enter Default Garment Information Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu File Information Garment The Garment Information window appears. Click the Edit icon on the right top corner of the window. The Garment Information window changed to the edit mode. Type in necessary information next to each category and click OK. Typed in information is saved. Add Category Refer to Enter Default Garment Information manual to active the edit mode. Click the Add icon. A category is added. Click the drop-down menu and select desired category. There are eight categories to choose from: Code, Name, Description, Price, Fabric, Size, Colorway, Category, and Memo. Type in necessary information for each category and click OK. Typed in information is saved. Reorder Category Refer to Enter Default Garment Information manual to active the edit mode. Click and drag the category to the desired position. The category is moved to where the mouse is released. When categories are re-ordered completely, click OK. Revised category order is saved. Delete Category Refer to Enter Default Garment Information manual to active the edit mode. Click the Delete icon next to each category. The selected category is deleted. When the editing is completed, click OK. The deleted category no longer appears in the Garment Information window. Note: Toggle on Display When Garment File Loads option to open the Garment Information window every time the file opens. Open or save Garment information such as categories, order, and contents by using the Open and Save buttons on the right top corner of the edit mode. Use the Default File setting to designate default Garment Information file.

Title: Avatar (*.avt) Open/Save
Content: Objective Save and load all Avatar related files, such as the Model (*.dae or *obj), Pose (*.pos), Motion (*.mtn), Accessories (*.acc), Bounding Volume (*.pan), and Arrangement Points (*.arr) as one file (*.avt). Location Open AVT Main Menu File Open Avatar (Ctrl+Shift+A) Save AVT Main menu File Save As Avatar Operation Open AVT Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu File Open Avatar (Ctrl+Shift+A) The Open File window appears. Select the desired file and click Open to load it. Note: The default avatars provided by Marvelous Designer are located in the following path. Windows Library Documents Marvelous Designer Assets_ver_x.x.x Avatar Avatar (Detail Path) C: Users User Name Documents Marvelous Designer Assets_ver_x.x.x Avatar Avatar Save AVT Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu File Save As Avatar The Open File window appears. Select a location to save the Garment file, enter in a name and press Save button. Note: Even if multiple Avatars exist within the workspace, they can be saved separately (ver2.3.0).

Title: 3D Garment Surface Textures - Save
Content: Objective Save all texture images used on Garments and subsidiary Materials to a designated folder. Surface textures can also be cropped to a desired size before they are saved (ver2.5.0). Location Main Menu File Save As Surface Textures Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu File Save As Surface Textures The Save File window appears. Select a Folder location to save the Surface Textures, then press Save. The Save Surface Textures window appears. Select from the available settings. Original Size Saves the surface textures in its original size. Crop Fabric Textures Crops the image file based on the value entered. Click OK. The selected image size setting is applied and the files are saved to the Folder location assigned. Note: Surface textures refers to the surface texture of a Garment.

Title: 3D Garment (*.zpac) Add
Content: Objective Add an extra Garment to the current Garment to coordinate. Location Main Menu File Add Garment Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu File Add Garment Select a Garment file and click Open. The Add Garment window appears (ver2.4.0.) Select the appropriate settings and click OK to place the Garment Note: A Garment can be added by right clicking on the Library's Garment file and using the Add to Workplace menu. Add Garment Settings Placement X Placement long the X axis, relative to the center of the 3D Window. Y Placement long the Y axis, relative to the center of the 3D Window. Z Placement long the Z axis, relative to the center of the 3D Window. Unit Unit for placement.

Title: [Mode] SCULPT
Content: Objective Sculpt garments using various brush tools. (ver. 8) Location SCULPT Mode Brush Tool Operation Select SCULPT mode on the menu select menu at the top right of Marvelous Designer. The Brush toolbar appears in the upper left corner of the SCULPT mode screen. Select a Brush tool from Brush toolbar. When mouseover on 3D garment after selecting a brush tool, can check brush Size and Focal setting. With a brush is selected, brush property will be displayed. Adjust Strenght, Size, Focal, Spacing Depth on Brush property. Also can change brush type and property setting on 3D window pop up menu (shortcut:B). Click and drag on 3D garment to sculpt. Press the Shift key on the keyboard while using any type of Brush tool. 3D garment will be displayed with gray in SCULPT mode. Adjust the color either material of 3D garment on Material Type on the property window. Brush Types Wrinkle Left-click and drag to create wrinkles on the brush area. (ver. 10) Release Left-click + Shift and drag to release wrinkles on brush area. (ver. 10) Sculpt Emboss mesh. With invert option activated, engraves mesh. Smooth Makes the surface flat on average. (Shortcut: Shift) Grab Moves vertexes to express pulled surface. Stamp Use an image as a stamp. Pinch Close the position of the vertexes, makes the surface sharper. Brush Property Depending on the type of brush, the properties you apply vary. Brush Property Description Brush Type Wrinkle Release Sculpt Smooth Grab Stamp Pinch Simulation Preset Simulation types that are applied when using Wrinkle and Release brush (ver. 10) O O X X X X X Strength Strength of brush. X X O O O O O Size Size of brush. O O O O O O O Focal Coverage of brush. (similar with Hardness) O O O O O O O Spacing Interval of brush. X X O X X X X Depth Depth of brush. X X O O O X O Invert Change the direction of a brush. (shortcut: Alt) X X O X X O X Image Using an image as brush. X X O X O O X Realistic Realistic (ver. 10) (Setting for Wrinkle, Release brush) O O X X X X X Layer Layer (ver. 10) (Setting for Wrinkle, Release brush) O O X X X X X Using an image as brush Click button next to Image. Click an Image from default images. - Focal setting is not available for image brush. Click &amp Drag on 3D garment to Sculpt. - Click &amp Drag to adjust the size and angle for Stamp brush. To turn off an image, click button and select Off. - Focal setting appears on brush property after turning off image. Adding image Click + button next to image. Select an image on the file browser. Click &amp Drag on 3D garment to Sculpt. - Click &amp Drag to adjust the size and angle for Stamp brush. After adding image, can load the image by clicking button next to the image. Creating image Image file should be Black and white (mono-tone). White area emboss when using it as a brush. Double Side Display With Double Side option activated, can check both back and front side of mesh. Show/Hide 3D Pattern (Shortcut Shift+Q) Show selected pattern only - Select a pattern while input Shift+Q, other patterns will be hidden. Reverse selected pattern/hidden pattern - After operating no.1 above, click on the selected pattern while input Shift+Q to reverse hidden pattern/ selected pattern. Adding hidden patterns - To hide additional patterns, click on a pattern which you want to hide while input Shift+Q. Show All 3D Patterns - Click on the background while input Shift+Q to show all pattern. 3D Garment Rendering Style You can set the following menus from the View Settings icon on the left of the 3D window. Show Internal Lines Monochrome Surface (Alt+3) / Wireframe on Surface (Alt+6)

Title: MODULAR MODE: Select a Block in the Modular Configurator Window
Content: Objective Select and combine Blocks as desired in the Modular Configurator window. Location Modular Mode Vertical Menu Tab on the Left Modular Configurator Operation 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Modular Mode Vertical Menu Tab on the Left Modular Configurator Modular Configurator window appears. 2. Select a desired category from the horizontal tab. Folders appear in order. 3. Select a desired Garment category folder. Modular Structure file is displayed. 4. Select a desired Modular Structure file. All Blocks compatible with the selected Module Structure are now being displayed. 5. Select a desired Block. The Blocks are replaced accordingly. 6. Modify the design as desired and complete the 3D Garment.

Title: MODULAR MODE: Edit Block Folders in the Modular Configurator Window
Content: Objective Edit Block folders at your convenience to organize Blocks in the folders. Location Vertical Menu Tab on the Left Modular Configurator (Select) Block Folder Operation 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Vertical Menu Tab on the Left Modular Configurator (Select) Block Folder All Blocks in the selected Block folder appears in the Modular Configurator. 2. Select the Edit button. Show icons appear on every Garment thumbnails. 3. Select a Modular Structure file that you want to organize first. All Blocks compatible with the selected Module Structure are now being displayed. 4. Click on the Display icon to either display or hide the Garments or Blocks Hidden Garments or Blocks appear in lighter shade and the displayed Garments or Blocks appear in brighter shade. 5. Click on the Save button to save in the configuration file in the same folder as the Block. 6. When editing is done, select the Exit button. The Blocks appear in the Modular Configurator accordingly. Note: It is able to tie the Modular configuration files as a group by adding a group in the Editor Mode when needing a category that is above all the Modular configuration files. Unlikely to the Blocks, one Modular configuration file can only be included in one group.

Title: MODULAR MODE: Add Block Folders in the Modular Configurator Window
Content: Objective Create and manage Modular Configurator categories and folders. Location Modular Mode Vertical Menu Tab on the Left Modular Configurator Operation Create Folders 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Modular Mode Vertical Menu Tab on the Left Modular Configurator Modular Configurator window appears. 2. Click on the (+) icon at top-right corner of the Configurator. Open Category window appears. 3. Select a folder. The selected folder appears in the Configurator. Rename Folders 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Modular Mode Vertical Menu Tab on the Left Modular Configurator Modular Configurator window appears. 2. Right click on the tab and click Rename. Rename window appears. 3. Rename folders. Delete Folders 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Modular Mode Vertical Menu Tab on the Left Modular Configurator Modular Configurator window appears. 2. Right click on the name of the category tab to delete. The category is now being deleted. Note: The Block files belong to the according category also gets deleted. Configurator Window Options Update Update any changes of the folders. Display Change folder file display.

Title: MODULAR MODE: Order of Use of the Modular Configurator Window
Content: Follow the order of use of the Modualr Configurator window in order to construct and use an user data. To create a configuration file for the Modular Configurator, please follow the steps below: Open the Modular Configurator window Add an User folder by pressing (+) icon Press the Edit icon to switch to the Editor Mode If needed, add groups by pressing Add Group icon Designate the Modular file (.zmdr) to either be displayed or hidden for each group Designate the Modular file (.zblc) to either be displayed or hidden for each group Click Save button to save the structure file in the same folder as the Block Press Exit button when editing is done

Title: MODULAR MODE: Sew Blocks
Content: Objective Set seamlines between Patterns and Block Boxes. Location Modular Mode Block Editor Operation Sew Patterns and Block Boxes 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Modular Mode Block Editor 2. Click on Segment sewing tool or Free sewing tool. 3. Set seamlines for Pattern and its relative Block Boxes (Step 2 and 3 do not necessarily need to be in order). 4.Set Pattern outlines (Patterns must be sewn one another i.e. shoulder seams, armholes, side seams) and seamlines between Block Boxes. 5. Repeat the steps above for the remains. Note: Block Boxes can only be sewn with Segment Sewing. In other words, sewing multiple Block Box segments at once by using M:N Free Sewing is not allowed. Therefore if the number of Block Box segments is higher than the number of segments need to be sewn, add segments on the patterns to make the number equal, then sew them 1:1. ex) In case of a basic t-shirt block, there is a point added on the neck segment. Therefore add a point on its pattern, then sew the segments 1:1. Patterns that are sewn alone (i.e. hems, sleeves or armholes of a sleeveless style) do not need to be sewn to Block Boxes. Difference in length between the actual Pattern and the Block Boxes has no effect on the simulation. Rest of the principle is the same as the Simulation Mode. Show Modular Sewing / Show Pattern Sewing 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Modular Mode Block Editor 2. 2D Toolbar default presets Show Modular Sewing / Show Pattern Sewing tool. While the tool is toggled on, it enables to check the seamlines between Patterns and Block Boxes. 3. Deselect Show modular sewing / Show pattern sewing tool. Block Boxes to Pattern seamlines disappears but for Patterns to Patterns are appeared. Note: If seamlines do not appear after setting Pattern and Block Boxes, please confirm Show modular sewing / Show pattern sewing toggle status.
